official.deadline_central_display: 27 February 2026 (2026 call closed; six weeks from publication on 18 January 2026)
official.application_cycle: 2026 Overseas Postgraduate Scholarship Scheme (call published 18 January 2026); the 2027 call has not been published
official.status_note: The official closing date for the 2026 scheme was 27 February 2026, six weeks after publication; PTDF has not yet published a 2027 call.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official wording: 'Tuition and bench fees (where applicable)' among the listed scholarship benefits.
benefits: Allowances for accommodation and living expenses
eligibility: Nigerian candidates for MSc or PhD at PTDF partner universities in the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Malaysia
MSc: minimum Second Class Upper (2:1) first degree, or Second Class Lower (2:2) with relevant industry experience
PhD: at least Second Class Lower (2:2) first degree plus a good postgraduate degree
Mandatory National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) completed
Five (5) O-Level credits including English Language and Mathematics
Verified National Identity Number (NIN) before application (NIMC verification charges apply)
Programme of study consistent with the applicant's prior academic background and relevant to the oil and gas industry
Candidates previously sponsored by the Fund for a scholarship category are ineligible to apply again for the same or lower category
requirements: Applications limited to PTDF-approved courses at PTDF partner institutions

2026 UK PhD awards are limited to split-site programmes at the College of Petroleum and Energy Studies, Kaduna (CPESK) with Robert Gordon University, University of Strathclyde or University of Portsmouth
PhD applicants under the PTDF/DAAD partnership in Germany must secure a research supervisor before the final selection interviews
Lecturers must submit a letter from their Vice-Chancellor confirming they are not benefiting from any other scholarship
MSc: Statement of Purpose of maximum 500 words covering rationale, relevance to the oil and gas industry and expected contribution to national development
PhD: research proposal of maximum five pages covering topic, introduction/background, objectives, methodology and data collection approach
documents: First Degree Certificate or Statement of Result
WAEC/GCE/SSCE/NECO results and the relevant PIN(s) for online verification
Evidence of membership of relevant professional associations
selection_criteria: Initial screening on submitted qualifications; top applicants in each category from each State invited to interview
Academic merit: quality of degrees, complete academic transcripts, relevant professional qualifications
Viability and relevance of the study plan / research proposal
Relevance of prior studies to the oil and gas industry and the proposed programme or research
coverage: Allowances for accommodation and living expenses
application_method: Create an applicant account on the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal at scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng and follow the email instructions to set a password
Complete the online application form and scan and upload clear copies of all mandatory documents
Shortlisted candidates attend a selection interview and must present transcripts in advance
official.application_route: Apply through the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal at scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng during the published call window (the 2026 call ran 18 January - 27 February 2026).
official.citizenship_residency: Nigerian citizens with a Certificate of Indigeneship / Local Government Identification Letter.
official.international_eligibility: Nigerian citizens only; the scheme funds study abroad at PTDF partner universities in the UK, Germany, France and Malaysia.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Only oil and gas related disciplines at PTDF partner institutions on the approved schools list; candidates may be disqualified for programmes deemed not relevant to the oil and gas industry.
official.research_requirement: PhD applicants must submit a research proposal relevant to the oil and gas industry, maximum five pages, and DAAD-partnership applicants must secure a research supervisor before final interviews.
official.description: The Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF), a Nigerian federal government agency responsible for developing indigenous human capacity and petroleum technology for the oil and gas sector, invites applications for fully funded overseas MSc and PhD scholarships at selected partner universities in the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Malaysia, providing access to world-class training, research facilities and global expertise.

applicant_utility.summary: This scheme pays for everything it lists - flights, health insurance, tuition and bench fees, accommodation and living allowances - but it is tightly gated: only Nigerian citizens who have completed NYSC and hold at least a 2:1 (or 2:2 with industry experience) can compete, and only for courses on PTDF's approved partner list. The application route rewards early administrative work: NIN verification, WAEC/NECO PINs ready for online checking, and a 500-word Statement of Purpose (MSc) or five-page proposal (PhD) that ties your study explicitly to the oil and gas industry. Because the Fund deliberately limits awards to fields relevant to its mandate, a persuasive relevance argument in your proposal matters as much as your grades.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Nigerian graduates with strong oil-and-gas-aligned degrees, completed NYSC, and clean documentation who want a funded MSc or PhD at a PTDF partner university in the UK, Germany, France or Malaysia.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your NIN on the NIMC platform and budget for the verification charge before the call opens
Retrieve your WAEC/GCE/SSCE/NECO results and PINs so exam bodies can be checked online
Confirm your intended course appears on the PTDF approved-schools list for overseas study before writing anything
Draft the Statement of Purpose (MSc, max 500 words) or research proposal (PhD, max five pages) months ahead - both have hard formats tied to industry relevance
Lecturers: request the Vice-Chancellor's 'no other scholarship' letter early, since it requires university sign-off
DAAD-track PhD applicants: identify and secure a German research supervisor before the final interview stage
common_rejection_risks: Submitting more than one application - this results in automatic disqualification
Proposing a programme PTDF judges not relevant to the oil and gas industry, or outside your prior academic background
Illegible or falsified documents - both are automatic disqualification grounds
Having been previously sponsored by the Fund at the same or a lower category
Applying for a UK PhD outside the CPESK split-site route, which was the only UK PhD structure for 2026
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The call does not specify stipend amounts or what the accommodation and living allowances actually cover, so budget personally for visa fees, NIMC verification charges, transcript procurement, relocation costs beyond the return ticket, and any expenses not itemised in 'tuition and bench fees (where applicable)'.
document_audit: O-Level results need their PINs kept handy - PTDF verifies WAEC/NECO results online during screening
PhD applicants need the master's degree certificate in addition to the first degree certificate
Evidence of professional body membership is mandatory, not optional, for all applicants
alerts: The call window is short - six weeks from publication to deadline - so waiting for the announcement to start gathering documents is too late
Interviews are state-quota based: only the top applicants per category per State are invited, so you compete nationally within your state
The 2027 call date has not been published; monitor scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng/news rather than relying on last year's January timing
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an account on scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng, complete the online form with PDF uploads during the call window, await qualification screening, then attend the interview stage (transcripts must be made available in advance) if shortlisted.
